observations: Crate density spikes in small rooms and drops to zero in timing corridors (smashers, icicles, bridges, disc rocks).
The 8 post-top crates exist only to make the player climb unstable footing among seals.
Explosives escalate from environment-lit TNT to TNT as weapon/springboard to Nitro on ice.
Switches are perception puzzles: an enemy kicked into a !, and four ! blocks hidden behind pillars.
Masks precede gauntlets; the death route recommends bringing one.
Checkpoints sit at camera-mode changes and at the death-route gate.
The perfect requires bonus, death route twice with a walk-back, hidden switches and the green ! last.
Main-route count unresolved: F2 drawing accounts for 76 of 103 implied boxes.

cameraSections.notes: diagonal snow canyon climbing away from the camera (F2 p067R draws it bottom-left to top-right); ice cliffs wall both sides; pits cut across the full width; ends in a vertical elevator shaft (D2 p059 shot 7).

left-to-right strips (F2 p068L, p068R strip A then strip B). The route climbs a crate stair to the bonus pad, drops to a room under an overhang, climbs switch-made steel steps, then steps down ice ledges to C2.
five alternating ice slides drop the route several storeys (F2 p068R strip B; D2 shot 21), then left to right along ice ledges and a smasher corridor to C3 (F2 p069L strip 1).
left to right (F2 p069R strip 1, p069L strip 2, p069R strip 2); ends by dropping back into the 3D view (F2 つづく↓; D2 shot 34).
climb bottom-left to top-right in a walled canyon (F2 p070L); a pit, a deep trench and further pits cut across the corridor; stone-disc channels cross it at right angles near the top.
same climb to the goal (F2 p070R): three more disc channels, steel stairs, two stump pillars.
entered from the green pillar pad in S2; the camera follows you down "level to level" (D2 shot 11).
green-lit ice cave entered by the skull elevator beside C2 (D2 shots 46–47); left to right; ends with a drop shaft to the gem (D2 59) or the ! block that lets you walk back (D2 60).

geometryObservations: Each camera grammar owns its own hazard family. The 3D canyon has pits with falling stumps and enemies that slide toward the camera. The side-scroll strips have smashers, icicles and collapsing bridges. The final 3D climb has disc rocks crossing the corridor, and the death route replays the side-scroll family on ice.

One hazard escalates four times. Smasher pair 1 teaches run-under/slide-under on a flat floor (O-S2-a). Pair 2 repeats it with less slack (O-S2-d). Three smashers on ice remove reliable stopping (O-S3-b). The five-smasher colonnade then inverts the rule, because waiting kills (O-S4-b). The death route finally combines smashers with Nitros (G-D-c).

Icicles teach bait-and-wait with a proximity trigger: walk close, stop short, let them fall, pass (O-S2-b). The same trigger then lights a TNT (O-S2-f) and later guards a seal on ice (O-D-b). One rule, three contexts.

Falling platforms escalate and then relent. The first stump stands alone (P-S1-b). The second has a spinning penguin on its landing (P-S1-f). The last one recovers after dropping, so the player can back off from a mistimed disc crossing (P-S5-f, POINT19). The most generous version comes just before the last checkpoint.

Ice multiplies everything and forces a commitment decision. Some places demand slowness: Nitro spacing in the trench and death route (F2 p099L), and smashers on ice (POINT10). Others demand full speed: the colonnade, where D2 33 says stopping or slowing is fatal. The player must read which.

Enemy archetype follows camera. In into-screen downhill stretches, enemies slide at you as projectiles (penguins and seals). In side-scroll strips, they stand on landing ledges or in recesses (penguins beside Nitros, porcupines in rooms). The final climb puts porcupines on pit rims, where facing direction decides when you cross.

The porcupine is taught in three geometries, and each limits your approach. In the closed recess you hug the wall and use him as a projectile (E-S2-a). In the low passage you lure him out (E-S3-d). On pit rims you cross while he faces away (E-S5-d, E-S6-a).

Explosive neighbours change enemy counters. A penguin is spun on open floor, but beside a Nitro or a TNT pile it must be stomped (E-S4-d, E-S5-c). Placing an enemy against an explosive is the cheapest way to make an old enemy a new test.

Rest is spaced by geometry rather than by empty floor. The wide pit banks in S1, the overhang ledge between Nitro ledges (P-S4-f) and the C5 island inside the disc field (P-S5-g) are the rests, and every checkpoint sits where the camera changes or a hazard family begins.

Non-lethal failure is reserved for precision tasks. A fall from the posts drops you among seals (G-S1-c), and a miss on the crate stair drops you to the floor (G-S2-c). Lethal gaps are kept short (≈1–3 u) and simple in shape.

Disc channels are crossing gates with a built-in perch. A ≈1-u curb lines each channel, so you can stand and watch the disc before committing (P-S5-d). The finale doubles the disc (O-S6-b), and the late channels put an enemy on the perch (E-S6-b).

Crates act as geometry throughout. The striped stair is the only way up to the bonus (P-S2-e). The TNT is a springboard in the bonus (G-B-a). Nitros shorten landings (O-S4-a) and mine stepping stones (O-S5-a). The arrow in the death route becomes a catapult trap (G-D-b).

The death route strips the level's verbs of safe footing. It has ice everywhere, smashers with Nitros under them, porcupines on small ledges and no checkpoint, since dying returns you to C2 (D2 59). Its single exit makes the gem goal and the box goal incompatible in one pass (G-D-d).
geometryTransfer: Smasher ladder: put four `crusher` set-pieces through one level, using `phase` offsets on a shared `cycle`. Start with a pair on flat ground offset by half a cycle (run under the first, slide under the second). Repeat the pair with tighter spacing, then three over a `slip` (icy) platform. Finish with a colonnade of five crushers ≈2 crates (≈2.3 m) apart over ≈11 crates (≈13 m). A 12 m/s skate cruise crosses it in ≈1.1 s and a 9 m/s run in ≈1.5 s, so step the phases ≈0.2–0.25 s apart so that only continuous motion passes, as in POINT15.

Disc channel: put a `stone` with `axis: "x"` in a trough 2–3 crates wide (≈2.3–3.5 m) so it rolls across the corridor, with a 1-crate curb on each side as a perch (and an edge grind for skaters). The crossing fits inside one full jump (≈5.6 m). For the finale, set two `stone`s in one trough half a patrol apart so they cross in the middle.

Falling stump sequence: use a `crumble` pad 1.5 crates wide (≈1.7 m) in the middle of a 3-crate (≈3.5 m) `pit`, with a short `shake` (≈0.3 s) so it "drops the moment you land". Use it alone first, then with a `spinner` on the landing bank. The engine's crumble already returns 10 s after dropping, which is POINT19's recovering stump: place that version before a moving hazard and tell the player they may retreat.

Nitro trench: lay narrow pillar tops 1–1.5 crates wide (≈1.2–1.7 m) in a `pit` trench, with Nitros on three of them in a 2 + 1 pattern. Clearing the adjacent pair needs ≈2.3–3.5 m of travel plus a landing, which is in full-jump range. A double jump (+1.74 m) gives the height margin. Keep skate lines out: the tap ollie (0.56 m) cannot clear a crate.

Icicle bait-and-wait has no proximity primitive here (`crusher` runs on a fixed `cycle`/`phase`). Approximate it with one slow-cycle `crusher` (≈3–4 s) just past a checkpoint, phased to drop as the player arrives, so the first lesson is "stop short, watch it fall, then pass". Do not rely on it to light a TNT: nothing measured shows a crusher detonating crates.
